S86.01.needs: none (linked social accounts need the outside account, e.g. Google)
S86.01.note: Settings opening path from sign-in was not traced; the Security nav label is from settings.json.
steps: Open Settings and choose Security.
Find the Sign-in methods section.
Check the Password row shows Set or Not set with a Change or Add button.
Check the Passkeys row and the list of linked sign-in accounts, each with a Remove button.
Compare with Expected: every sign-in way is shown and can be added or removed.

S86.02.needs: an outside email account to receive the reset link
S86.02.note: The reset link is on the signed-out sign-in page, not in Settings; the email step itself was not traced.
steps: Open Settings > Security.
In Sign-in methods, click Change on the Password row (or Add if none is set).
Look for the Current Password, New Password and Confirm Password fields and the Change Password button.
Compare with Expected: a password can be changed with the current password.
Sign out, then on the sign-in page click Forgot password? and compare with Expected: a forgotten password can be reset.
S86.02.where: Settings > Security > Sign-in methods > Password (Change or Add)

S86.03.needs: a Desktop app build (per plan); a device that can make a passkey
S86.03.note: The rename button label was not confirmed as a literal string; the rename handler exists in PasskeysPanel.tsx.
steps: Open Settings > Security.
Find the Passkeys section (the Passkeys row in Sign-in methods lists the count).
Click Add a passkey to add one, then check it appears in the list with its created and last-used dates.
Click Rename on a passkey, change the name, and save.
Click Remove on a passkey and confirm; compare with Expected: each action works.

S86.04.needs: an authenticator app on a phone
steps: Open Settings > Security and find the Authenticator app section.
Click Enable two-factor and confirm the prompt.
Enter the code from your authenticator app and check that two-factor shows On.
Sign out and sign in again: a code from the authenticator app is asked for.
Return to Authenticator app and click Turn off two-factor to compare with Expected: it can be turned off.

labels.text: I have saved these backup codes somewhere safe

S86.05.needs: an authenticator app with two-factor already on
S86.05.note: No view or download control for existing codes was found in the searched file.
steps: Open Settings > Security > Authenticator app.
Click Generate new backup codes (or Replace backup codes if codes exist) and confirm.
Read the new codes shown, tick I have saved these backup codes somewhere safe, and continue.
Compare with Expected: codes are shown once and the old codes stop working.
Check whether the codes can be viewed or downloaded again; this was not confirmed in the code.
S86.05.where: Settings > Security > Authenticator app > Replace backup codes or Generate new backup codes

S86.06.needs: a second signed-in device or browser to end a session
steps: Open Settings > Security and click the Active sessions row.
On the Account page, read each session row: device, place and last active.
Click Revoke on a session other than the current one and confirm Revoke session.
Compare with Expected: the chosen session is ended and removed from the list.
S86.06.where: Settings > Security > Active sessions (opens Settings > Account session list)

S86.07.needs: a linked device such as the desktop app or the Chrome extension
S86.07.note: The code shows no separate trusted-device list that skips checks; trust appears only as linked devices. The Security page also has a device sign-in toggle (DeviceSignInToggle) that was not traced.
steps: Open Settings > Account and scroll to Linked devices.
Read the list of linked devices (CLI, VS Code, Chrome extension, desktop app).
Click Unlink on one device, then Unlink device in the prompt.
Compare with Expected: the device is removed and its access is revoked when it next connects.

S86.08.needs: the Desktop app; a paid plan for Remote Control; the Chrome extension for browser pairing
S86.08.note: Remote Control shows a phone-pairing flow with a Stop control; the exact Stop label was not located.
steps: Open Settings > Capabilities and find the Remote Control section.
Click Pair a phone to see the pairing code, then cancel or close it.
Find the Chrome section and read whether the browser is paired.
Click Unpair, then Unpair in the prompt.
Compare with Expected: the paired device is listed and can be unpaired.
S86.08.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control (Pair a phone) and Settings > Capabilities > Chrome (Unpair)

S86.09.note: The app menu or other sign-out entry points were not searched.
steps: Open Settings > Security and click Active sessions to reach the Account session list.
Find the row marked as this device (current session).
Click Log out on that row and confirm Log out this session?.
Compare with Expected: this device or app is signed out.
S86.09.where: Settings > Account > Active sessions row marked current > Log out

S86.10.needs: a second signed-in device or browser to confirm it ends
steps: Open Settings > Security.
Find the row Log out of all devices and click its Log out button.
Read the prompt Log out of all devices? and click Log out everywhere.
Compare with Expected: every browser and app is signed out, including this one.
On another device, check that its session has ended.
S86.10.where: Settings > Security > Log out of all devices

S86.11.needs: an email address on the account
S86.11.note: The individual toggle labels were not read; only the group heading was confirmed.
steps: Open Settings > Notifications.
Find the Security alerts group (sign-in, password, email, two-factor and device changes).
Change a control for Security alerts and close the panel.
Reopen it and check the choice was kept.
Trigger a security event (e.g. a password change) and compare with Expected: a notice arrives by the chosen channel.

S86.12.needs: a connector already connected (e.g. GitHub or Slack)
S86.12.note: The disconnect button's exact visible label was not located in the connector files searched.
steps: Open Settings > Connectors.
Read the list of connected accounts.
Open a connected account and find its disconnect action.
Click it and confirm; compare with Expected: the account is disconnected and no longer listed.
Open Settings > Connectors.
Open a connected account.
Find the Permissions granted list.
Compare with Expected: the granted permissions for that account are shown.
S86.13.where: Settings > Connectors > (a connected account) > Permissions granted

S86.14.needs: none (a plan that allows API keys may be required)
S86.14.note: The revoke control's visible label was not located.
steps: Open Settings > Account and click API keys.
Click Generate New API Key, type a name, and submit.
Copy the key shown once and close it.
Check the list shows the key masked with a Created date.
Find a Revoke action on a key and compare with Expected: keys can be revoked.

S86.16.needs: the Desktop app; at least one folder added
S86.16.note: The control for adding a folder was not located.
steps: Open Settings > Capabilities and find the Local access section.
Read the Folders list.
Click Remove access next to a folder and confirm.
Compare with Expected: the folder is removed and AGI can no longer read or write in it.

S86.18.needs: the Desktop app (Electron); macOS accessibility permission for control
S86.18.note: Add app is in the refused-apps picker; the control to add an allowed app was not located.
steps: Open Settings > Computer use.
Read the Allowed apps list.
Click Add app under Refused apps to refuse an app, then check it appears.
Click Stop if an action is running and compare with Expected: AGI stops controlling the app.

S86.19.note: Mapped in the permission labels; the row rendering was not fully traced.
steps: Open Settings > Capabilities and find Local access.
Find the Permissions list and locate Read the clipboard.
Change the choice or remove it, then compare with Expected: AGI's clipboard access follows that choice.
S86.19.where: Settings > Capabilities > Local access > Permissions > Read the clipboard

S86.22.needs: the Desktop app; macOS screen recording permission
S86.22.note: The nav label General is shared with the main General section, and the Capture the screen permission is under Permissions.
steps: Open Settings > General (desktop section).
Find the Screenshot to chat shortcut and Window to chat shortcut rows.
Change or clear a shortcut.
Press the shortcut and compare with Expected: only the chosen capture happens.
S86.22.where: Settings > General > Screenshot to chat shortcut

S86.23.needs: the Desktop app; a saved approval (answer Always allow once first)
S86.23.note: A second Permissions heading exists under Capabilities > Local access.
steps: Open Settings > General and scroll to Permissions.
Read each saved answer; it shows Always allowed, Allowed once, or Allowed until you quit the app.
Click Remove (or Ask again on a refused one) and confirm.
Compare with Expected: the saved approval is gone and AGI asks again next time.

S86.24.needs: none; Skip approvals needs a workspace that allows it
S86.24.note: Skip approvals is disabled with Your workspace does not allow skipping approvals. when the workspace blocks it.
steps: Open Settings > Capabilities and find Tool approvals.
Read the radio group Default approval for tool actions: Ask before every action, Run read-only actions without asking, Skip approvals.
Select Run read-only actions without asking, then start an agent action and check it runs without a prompt for read-only steps.
Select Ask before every action and check it asks again.

S86.26.needs: a passkey or security key; an email address
S86.26.note: The exact effects of hardened mode were not traced beyond the panel.
steps: Open Settings > Security and find the Advanced Account Security section.
Click Turn on Advanced Account Security.
Confirm with one of your passkeys or security keys when asked.
Check the on state and the notice that a link turns it off within the undo window.
Compare with Expected: the stronger settings apply to the account.
S86.26.where: Settings > Security > Advanced Account Security > Turn on Advanced Account Security
